correctness.rationale: Orthogonally reducing dark/bright decomposition and strict dissipativity on the bright complement give an exact survival projection for any two positive rates. Walsh spectral decomposition gives the two-by-two Gram matrix in each eigenspace. Rank endpoints are one; at antipodal r all ranks are one; otherwise every interior k has both Walsh signs, forcing rank two. Exact Gram inversion gives the sitewise Krawtchouk formula. The degree-one Walsh eigenspace supplies necessary and sufficient zero-survival sites. Independent exact computations matched 640 instances d=2..6, and five non-Hermitian dynamics comparisons; these finite checks are not used as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The established one-trap spectral-projection method is fully credited. Its application to two independent sink vectors is not by itself novel, but the exact all-separation rank dichotomy, all-site Krawtchouk rational kernel and complete unit-capture classification require additional Walsh Gram-rank and degree-one sign arguments not stated in inspected primary treatments. Published-result queries produced no equivalent claim; absence of a hit is not a uniqueness guarantee.
residual_risks: Published semantic research records cannot rule out an equivalent independently obtained formula elsewhere or unpublished findings.
The full Razzoli et al. 2021 document was not systematically read following a journal rate limit, although its declared model has one trap.

Generic invariant-subspace methods could make some parts derivable for knowledgeable readers; the asserted original content is the complete evaluated two-sink classification and exact sitewise kernel, not the generic method.

value.rationale: Absorber placement is a concrete design degree of freedom for coherent transport. The theorem classifies all placements, shows the unique antipodal spectral redundancy (no gain at all from the second absorber), quantifies the other placements as d-1 new absorbing dimensions, and supplies rational capture probabilities for every localized start, including complete-capture antipodal shadows. This is a motivated global structure theorem, not a small numerical gain.
